r1-dependency-2.summary: Retrieved dependency mapping for kyc-service and mobile-bff, along with all recent changes across services over the past 7 days prior to the incident.

findings.statement: kyc-service calls kyc-vendor and user-db synchronously.
kyc-service was deployed with version v5.3.0 on 2026-10-17T17:30:00+00:00.
orders-service and fraud-service were deployed shortly before the incident onset on 2026-10-18.

open_questions: Did the deployment of kyc-service v5.3.0 on October 17 introduce the thread exhaustion issue observed around 13:50?
Is kyc-vendor experiencing elevated latency or outages leading to thread saturation in kyc-service?

r1-observability-1.summary: kyc-service experienced latency spikes and error rate surges starting at 13:51/13:52 due to external kyc-vendor 504 Gateway Timeouts, leading to verification worker pool exhaustion (64/64 busy) and concurrent error rate increases in mobile-bff.

findings.statement: kyc-service latency_p99_ms began rising sharply at 13:51, peaking at over 30 seconds.
kyc-service error_rate_pct anomaly started at 13:52, peaking at 42.72%.
mobile-bff error_rate_pct anomaly started at 13:52, rising up to 2.85%.
First warning of kyc-vendor returning 504 Gateway Timeout occurred at 13:50:15.
First kyc-service verification worker pool exhaustion error occurred at 13:53:03.
kyc-service CPU, memory, and pod restarts showed no anomalies or restarts during the incident window.

open_questions: What caused kyc-vendor to begin returning 504 Gateway Timeouts starting at 13:50?

r2-observability-1.summary: Verification of kyc-vendor telemetry shows no metrics anomaly, error rate increase, or latency spike during the incident window. While kyc-service experiences gateway timeouts calling kyc-vendor, the vendor's own RPS, error rate, and p99 latency remain completely normal.

findings.statement: kyc-vendor rps shows no anomaly during the incident window with a baseline of 24.61 req/s and stable values.
kyc-vendor error_rate_pct shows no anomaly during the incident window, staying at a baseline of 0.34% and maxing out at 0.48%.
kyc-vendor latency_p99_ms shows no anomaly during the incident window, maintaining a baseline of 716.88 ms.
No direct logs are available for kyc-vendor as it is an external service.

open_questions: Why does kyc-service experience gateway timeouts when calling kyc-vendor if kyc-vendor metrics show no degradation?

r2-observability-2.summary: kyc-service experienced thread and worker pool exhaustion starting at 13:53 UTC, directly caused by 30-second gateway timeouts from the external kyc-vendor POST /v2/pan/verify API that began at 13:50 UTC.

findings.statement: kyc-service logged 504 Gateway Timeout responses from kyc-vendor POST /v2/pan/verify after 30000ms starting at 13:50.
kyc-service latency p99 anomaly started upward at 13:51, reaching a peak of 30701.44ms at 14:24.
kyc-service error rate anomaly started at 13:52, rising to 42.72% at 13:53.
kyc-service logged verification worker pool exhaustion (64/64 busy) starting at 13:53.
mobile-bff error rate anomaly started at 13:52, reaching 2.85% at 14:27 due to downstream kyc-service failures.

open_questions: Why did kyc-vendor start returning 504 Gateway Timeouts for pan/verify starting at 13:50?

hypotheses.title: Third-party KYC Vendor Outage
hypotheses.mechanism: External third-party KYC vendor experienced intermittent routing or proxy gateway timeouts (returning 504 Gateway Timeouts) between their load balancer and origin servers, while their overall aggregate RPS, error rate, and p99 metrics remained outwardly stable. This blocked synchronous verification threads in kyc-service, exhausted its worker pool (64/64 busy), and caused errors in kyc-service and mobile-bff.

supporting.note: First warning of kyc-vendor returning 504 Gateway Timeout at 13:50:15, preceding all symptoms.
kyc-service retrying pan/verify calls due to vendor timeouts.
Verification worker pool exhaustion error in kyc-service resulting from blocked synchronous calls.
kyc-service latency p99 spiked dramatically starting at 13:51.
mobile-bff error rate concurrently rose at 13:52 due to synchronous dependencies on kyc-service.

contradicting.note: kyc-vendor RPS showed no anomaly during the incident window.
kyc-vendor error_rate_pct showed no anomaly during the incident window.
kyc-vendor latency_p99_ms showed no anomaly during the incident window.

assumptions: The external third-party kyc-vendor experienced localized gateway/proxy failures or upstream database lockups that manifested as 504 Gateway Timeouts at the API integration layer without registering as global metric anomalies.

hypotheses.title: KYC Service Deployment Regressed Timeout Handling
hypotheses.mechanism: The release of kyc-service v5.3.0 on October 17 introduced altered connection timeout parameters, overly aggressive retry loops, or inefficient payload formatting for the new PAN verification flow. This caused incoming requests to hang waiting on vendor responses longer than expected, ultimately triggering thread exhaustion under normal traffic loads.

supporting.note: kyc-service v5.3.0 deployed a new PAN verification screen flow a day prior to the incident.
Worker pool exhaustion occurred in kyc-service.

contradicting.note: Directly attributes the 30000ms timeouts to kyc-vendor POST /v2/pan/verify returning 504 Gateway Timeout rather than internal kyc-service logic.
kyc-vendor metrics remain entirely normal, making pure client-side triggering less likely.

assumptions: The 504 Gateway Timeout logs reported by kyc-service were triggered by internal connection pool starvation or client-side timeout misconfigurations in v5.3.0 rather than an actual server-side infrastructure failure at the vendor.

hypotheses.reasoning_summary: Addressing the Critic's point regarding kyc-vendor telemetry: specialized observability checks were conducted on kyc-vendor, showing that its aggregate rps, error_rate_pct, and latency_p99_ms remained completely normal during the incident window. This creates a strong contradiction for H1 (Vendor Outage), dropping its confidence. However, kyc-service explicitly logs 504 Gateway Timeouts from kyc-vendor POST /v2/pan/verify (log-00675), and kyc-vendor metrics alone do not rule out localized proxy gateway issues or downstream database stalls at the vendor. H2 (Bad Deploy, chg-8017) remains a viable alternative explaining worker pool exhaustion, though it conflicts with the explicit 504 timeout logs pointing outward. Both hypotheses are maintained with adjusted confidences reflecting the newly retrieved vendor metrics.

issues: The top hypothesis H1 attributes the failure to kyc-vendor returning 504 Gateway Timeouts, but no telemetry (logs or metrics) was retrieved for kyc-vendor to verify its health.
